The Problem

Access is stuck in the
hardware era.

  • ✕Hardware-locked & siloed. Doors, rooms, lockers, bookings and visitor access each run on their own island.
  • ✕Manual guest access. Every booking means someone cutting a key, sending a code, meeting at a front desk.
  • ✕No portfolio visibility. Operators can't see who went where, across every site, in real time.
  • ✕Spaces don't earn. Gates, lockers and amenities sit idle with no way to sell access on demand.
The gap

The lock got smart.
The software didn't.

Buildings went keyless, but the systems behind them stayed fragmented, manual, and blind to what's happening across the portfolio.

Competitive Landscape

Everyone overlaps one axis.
No one owns the intersection.

The threats cluster in three tiers — but none combine convergence, mid-market vertical depth and Australian data sovereignty.

Tier 1 · Convergent cloud platforms

The strategic threat

Verkada ($5.8B, 6 product lines), Avigilon Alta (Motorola), Genea, Coram.

Well-funded and converging — but enterprise-priced, camera-led and largely proprietary. Chasing up-market, not parks or childcare.

Tier 2 · Access & lock specialists

Closest head-to-head

Salto (locks + Gantner lockers + KS booking), Brivo (vacation-rental / multifamily), Kisi (gyms & coworking).

Overlap Rooms, Lockers & Spaces — but Salto needs its own hardware, and each still sells one module.

Tier 3 · ANZ incumbents

Who you meet in AU deals

Inner Range (Integriti), Gallagher, ICT, ZKTeco.

Hardware + on-prem, installer-led, high-security. Integriti is a partner surface we layer on — Gallagher's gov end we deliberately exclude.

Point solutions we replace on attach: Eagle Eye / Rhombus / Spot AI (video), Traka / Vecos (lockers), Envoy / Robin / Skedda (visitor & booking). Customers stitch these together today — convergence is the wedge.
